links.comparator_used: Manual clinician panel review (reference standard) of eligibility and condition mapping
links.outcome: Agreement with clinician review on eligibility classification and condition mapping, and resulting DDSS diagnostic accuracy estimates
links.effect: Eligibility: GPT-5 reproduced clinician classifications with 84.7% accuracy (κ = 0.57). Condition mapping: in 347 encounters judged eligible by both, GPT-5 exactly matched clinician diagnoses in 93.6% and proposed clinically plausible alternatives in 3.5%. DDSS accuracy based on manual vs GPT-5 mappings was statistically indistinguishable at Top-1 and Top-3, with one significant difference at Top-5; no differences in the overlapping 346 cases.
links.tradeoff: Eligibility filtering showed high sensitivity but only moderate specificity and remains the main source of divergence from clinicians; no cost or time figures reported.
links.quote: Diagnostic accuracy estimates based on manual versus GPT-5 mappings were statistically indistinguishable at Top-1 and Top-3 across the full analyzable sets, with one significant difference at Top-5.

design_hint: LLM-automated post-deployment performance monitoring vs manual clinician review
